sources.citation: Scruggs, Terri R. 1980. Segmental phonology of nouns in Yamba. MA thesis, University of Calgary, x+90 pp. -- only the 3-page Rosetta Project excerpt (ch. 2 'Phonemic system' intro + consonant and vowel feature tables) is open; full thesis restricted in Calgary Vault (doi:10.11575/PRISM/13229) and 'not available online' at SIL archive 9476.

sources.note: Excerpt says nothing on stress ('Most noun morphemes in Yamba are monosyllabic'); rest of thesis not accessible.

sources.citation: Nebup, Abraham Nwizine (comp.) & Robert Hedinger (ed.). 2019. Yamba Dictionary (Yamba-English), community-reviewed draft. Yamba Language Committee / SIL Cameroon, Webonary.org -- Introduction, Alphabet, Phonology and Grammar pages (read via r.jina.ai reader and a web.archive.org snapshot; site itself Cloudflare-blocked).
sources.note: Alphabet page: 'Low tone as in, nàm – animal. High and mid tones are unmarked... Rising tone is indicated by writing a double vowel' plus tone minimal pairs; Phonology page is only a reference list (Anderson 2001; Bradley 1986, 1995, 2007; Scruggs 1980a,b). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Nassuna Nzenge, Lucia. 2001. Yamba: a morphosyntactic study of the basic sentence. Mémoire de maîtrise (MA), Université de Yaoundé I. vi+87 pp. (Language Description Heritage open copy, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-8048-F)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.5.1 (pp. 14-16) reviews Scruggs 1980 and Bradley 1991: consonant/vowel graphemes, 'This orthographic system includes tones of which she indicates five' (p.14), Table 5 'Yamba Tones', Table 6 syllable types (V, CV, CCV, CCVC, CVC, CCCV); ch. 3 discusses a floating-H associative tone. No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole thesis.

sources.note: Phoneme/grapheme chart only; 'Tones: high, mid, low, rising' with marking conventions. Nothing on stress.
